overview: This file documents Japanese military intelligence-gathering and propaganda activities in Germany during 1932–1933, as observed by U.S. diplomatic and consular officials. Its records cover suspected Japanese army officers inspecting specialized German industrial machinery, reports of German war-material shipments to Japan, and extensive German-language publications defending Japan’s intervention in Manchuria. Later documents examine Japanese diplomatic personnel in Berlin, increasingly anti-American comments attributed to embassy staff, and a Japanese Club bulletin defending Japan’s naval construction under the Washington and London treaties.
interest: German-language pamphlets show how Japan defended Manchuria and naval policy to Europeans; US reports record diplomats' suspicions.
